items.title: Review: The New Congress Must Rein in Trump’s Dangerous China Policy
items.summary: Trump’s accommodating approach toward China has emboldened Beijing, but the new Congress has a rare chance to change course.

items.title: Review: Fall in China Demand May Signal Need for Easing: Analyst
items.summary: BofA Global Research Chief Greater China Economist Helen Qiao said the Chinese economy could see a further deterioration of domestic demand. China’s growth weakened across the board in October as consumption and industrial output undershot estimates while investment unexpectedly worsened, in a sign Beijing’s latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: MTN in Talks to Buy Telkom in South African Cash, Share Deal
items.summary: MTN Group Ltd. is in talks that could see Africa’s biggest wireless carrier buy all shares in Telkom SA SOC Ltd.

items.title: Review: How Could a Router Lead to a Nationwide Ground Stop?
items.summary: Aviation experts and federal officials said the network outage began after a new piece of networking equipment began flooding the rest of the system with data. The underlying cause is unclear.

items.title: Review: EQT Sees “Wave” of Take-Private Opportunities in Japan
items.summary: Jean Eric Salata, Chair at EQT Group, says the Stockholm-based private equity firm plans to invest up to 30 percent of its $30 billion in dry powder in Japan. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: Philippines Seeks New Equilibrium With China
items.summary: Philippine Ambassador to China Jaime FlorCruz says President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will travel to China for the APEC meetings as Manila seeks a “predictable” equilibrium with Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: A Year On, Canada’s Mark Carney Returns to China a Political Star
items.summary: Canada’s leader is courting Europe, but the bigger payoff might be in Asia, where he will share summit stages with Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and President Trump.

items.title: Review: They Defeated a Strongman. But Can They Run a Country?
items.summary: Serbia’s student movement was deliberately leaderless and made group decisions to unseat Aleksandar Vucic. Now no one seems quite sure what happens next.

items.title: Review: International Students Are Turning Away From U.S. Universities
items.summary: For a second year, Trump administration policies appear to be scaring away international students, disrupting the finances of the American colleges that depend on them.

items.title: Review: Chinese Iron Ore Futures Hit Four-Year Low on Weak Steel Outlook
items.summary: Chinese iron ore futures slumped to the lowest in four years as traders turned increasingly bearish on the demand outlook for winter.

items.title: Review: Apple launches an AI health tool as part of a research study
items.summary: On Sunday, Apple announced a new approach, launching the Apple Health AI Usage Study app that they say will answer health questions only using trusted medical research.

items.title: Review: Aerospace Stocks Shine as Anti-AI Flows Pour Into India
items.summary: A global aircraft shortage is pushing more aerospace work toward India.

items.title: Review: Airbus, Boeing Supply-Chain Shift Boosts India Aerospace Stocks
items.summary: A group of little-known Indian companies has emerged among the country’s best-performing stocks this year, powered by a multibillion dollar shift in global aerospace sourcing by Airbus SE and Boeing Co.

items.title: Review: Indonesia Says 70% of Benefits From Mines Should Go to State
items.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said most of the benefits of mining permits should accrue to the state, the latest move to tighten government control over the country’s natural resources.

items.title: Review: Chinese Aluminum Output Drops But Still on Course for Record
items.summary: Chinese aluminum output moderated last month as export demand softened and the industry runs up against Beijing’s capacity limits.
